The **angular insertion angle (AIA)** describes the trajectory/angle at which a cochlear implant electrode array is inserted into the scala tympani during surgery. This affects:
- How deep the electrode can be placed before hitting critical structures
- Whether the electrode will encounter the facial nerve or chorda tympani
- Surgical risk and approach selection

**What CochleaHub provides for ZETA:**

| Parameter | Value | Unit | Source | Notes |
|-----------|-------|------|--------|-------|
| Facial Nerve → Scala Tympani distance | 1.18 mm | [S31] | run 19ac527c, v0.1.0 | Critical for surgical approach |
| Chorda Tympani → Scala Tympani distance | 3.65 mm | [S33] | run 19ac527c, v0.1.0 | Branch point is at 0 mm |
| Cochlea A (diameter) | 8.97 mm | [S39] | run 19ac527c, v0.1.0 | In published range (8.17–9.33 mm) |
| Cochlea B (width) | 6.81 mm | [S40] | run 19ac527c, v0.1.0 | In published range (5.73–7.50 mm) |
| Cochlea height | 4.36 mm | [S41] | run 19ac527c, v0.1.0 | **Outside** published range (2.80–3.72 mm) |

**Important caveats:**
- AIA itself is not measured in this dataset; the distances above inform surgical planning but do not give the angle directly
- Cochlea dimensions use a landmark-free proxy (scala tympani oriented bounding box), not the clinical landmark method [S44]
- This data comes from one cadaveric specimen (ZETA); published ranges are from 36 ears of implant candidates aged 2–17 years [S39]
- CochleaHub is a research tool; it does not recommend treatment for patients

**For clinical decisions:** The treating surgical team should use these measurements alongside patient-specific imaging and established CDL formulas to plan the electrode length and insertion trajectory.
